R299.note: File I/O is removed entirely so the vector is closed, but the file-backed config is replaced by three invented keys with made-up rates; any real rate-config key the original resolved now throws KeyNotFoundException, and the write-up presents the table as given rather than as a placeholder to populate.

R300.note: RFC 4515 escaping of * ( ) backslash and NUL before concatenation closes the filter injection; legitimate cn values search identically.

R301.note: Dropping the template.HTML wrapper and typing Body as string restores html/template's contextual escaping; nothing else changes.

R302.note: CGI::escapeHTML on the subject at the sink closes the reflected XSS; priority and ticket_id are correctly left alone as constrained values.

R303.note: Resolving base and candidate and checking is_relative_to blocks absolute and ../ escapes; simple filenames behave as before and 404 handling is preserved.

R304.note: Named HQL parameter with the wildcards applied to the bound value is the correct Hibernate fix and preserves the contains-search semantics.

R305.note: Gate::authorize throws AuthorizationException (403) on denial, which is the framework's enforcing form of the ignored Gate::allows call.

R306.note: CSRFProtect plus FlaskForm/validate_on_submit closes the CSRF hole, but legitimate submissions now fail unless account_settings.html (not shown) renders form.csrf_token or hidden_tag(), and the write-up does not say the template must be updated.

R307.note: Parameterised @Owner via SqlCommand.Parameters closes the injection with no change to results for legitimate owners.

R308.note: Extension allowlist after secure_filename is the appropriate CWE-434 control, matches the docstring's document-only contract, and the chosen set is stated plainly as a product decision.

R309.note: Allowlist mapping of verbs to fixed handler names is the right shape, but the three verbs and handleXCommand names are invented (no handlers exist in the case), so any real command outside that guessed set now returns Unknown command and the write-up does not flag the mapping as needing population from the actual handlers.

R310.note: jwt.verify closes the signature check, but the hard-coded fallback secret 'your-secret-key' is a new weakness: the original never read JWT_SECRET so an existing deployment likely lacks it, in which case admin tokens are forgeable with the public constant instead of failing closed.

R311.note: realpath on base and target plus a path.relative containment check closes traversal and symlink escape; missing files still map to 404 and legitimate names are unaffected.

R312.note: resolve plus isAbsolute plus path.relative closes the traversal, but relativePath.startsWith('..') without a separator also rejects a legitimate in-directory file whose name begins with '..', an over-broad check the write-up does not mention.

R313.note: sqlite3 ? placeholder with a bound tuple is the correct parameterisation and preserves the query's results.

R314.note: Parameterised logging with repr() neutralises newlines and control characters; the resulting quoting of every username is stated in the write-up and blocks nothing.

R315.note: secure: true closes CWE-614; the added sameSite: 'lax' is stated extra hardening that still permits the top-level SSO redirect flow.
